RV and Camper Disposal Options

Whether you’re downsizing, upgrading, or simply ready to say goodbye to an old RV or camper, figuring out the best disposal method can feel overwhelming. Luckily, there are several routes you can take—each with its own set of benefits, costs, and environmental impacts. Below, we break down the most common options and show how partnering with a professional junk removal service like 1-800-GOT-JUNK? can make the whole process painless.

1. Donate Your RV or Camper

Donating is the gold standard for environmentally conscious disposal. Many nonprofit organizations accept RVs and campers, refurbish them, and then provide them to families in need, veterans, or charitable programs.

Who Accepts Donations?

  • Habitat for Humanity ReStore: Some locations take large vehicles for parts or resale.
  • Veterans’ Organizations: Groups like the Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) or local VA hospitals may accept RVs for housing veterans.
  • Nonprofit Resale Shops: Organizations that specialize in used goods often have the space and expertise to handle large items.

Before you donate, call the organization to confirm they have the capacity and the proper paperwork (like a tax receipt). Benefits of Donating

  • Potential tax deduction (keep the receipt!)
  • Reduces waste in landfills
  • Helps a charitable cause

2. Sell or Trade‑In Your RV

If the vehicle is still roadworthy, selling it privately or trading it in at a dealership can recoup a portion of your investment. Platforms like Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and RV-specific forums are popular for private sales.

Things to Keep in Mind

  • Condition: Ensure the RV is clean, mechanically sound, and has a clear title.
  • Pricing: Research recent sales of similar models to set a realistic price.
  • Paperwork: Transfer the title, registration, and any warranties correctly.

If you’re not comfortable handling the logistics—like removing the vehicle from a cramped driveway—consider a professional service. 1-800-GOT-JUNK? offers flexible removal plans that can take the RV off your hands, whether you’ve already sold it or need a quick solution. 3. Recycle or Scrap the Vehicle

When an RV or camper is beyond repair, recycling is the most responsible way to dispose of it. Metal components, tires, and certain plastics can be reclaimed and turned into new products.

Recycling Process

  1. De‑registration: Cancel the vehicle’s registration with your local DMV.
  2. Pick‑up: Contact a licensed scrap yard or a junk removal company that specializes in large vehicles.
  3. Disassembly: The yard will strip the RV of usable parts, recycle metal, and properly dispose of hazardous materials.

Because RVs are bulky, many scrap yards won’t accept the whole vehicle without assistance. 5. DIY Disposal (Not Recommended)

In some jurisdictions, you can tow the RV yourself to a local landfill or dump. However, this route often involves:

  • Heavy permits and fees
  • Special equipment (flatbed trailer, winch)
  • Potential fines for improper disposal
